```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(Cohort2Trajectory)
```

This synthetic example builds weekly trajectories with four analyst-defined
states: alive without recorded pneumonia, alive with pneumonia history, death
without that history, and death with it. The two death states are mutually
exclusive. They describe recorded history, not the cause of death.

The package does not construct these clinical definitions. Here we supply their
intervals directly. In a database study, the analyst would define equivalent
state cohorts. The target interval ends at death or the end of observation in
this example.

## Five patient histories

All patients enter on January 1, 2020. The examples cover:

- `001`: three weeks without pneumonia.
- `002`: pneumonia recorded on January 9, with history retained to observation end.
- `003`: pneumonia on January 10 and death on January 12, in the same weekly cycle.
- `004`: death without pneumonia history on January 4.
- `005`: observation ending on January 10, partway through the second cycle.

```{r input}
states <- c(
  "Alive, no recorded pneumonia",
  "Alive, pneumonia history",
  "Death, no pneumonia history",
  "Death, pneumonia history"
)

interval <- function(id, state, start, end) {
  data.frame(
    subject_id = id,
    cohort_definition_id = state,
    cohort_start_date = as.Date(start),
    cohort_end_date = as.Date(end)
  )
}

input <- do.call(rbind, list(
  interval("001", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("001", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("002", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("002", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-08"),
  interval("002", states[2], "2020-01-09", "2020-01-15"),
  interval("002", states[2], "2020-01-12", "2020-01-21"),
  interval("003", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-12"),
  interval("003", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-09"),
  interval("003", states[2], "2020-01-10", "2020-01-11"),
  interval("003", states[4], "2020-01-12", "2020-01-12"),
  interval("004", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-04"),
  interval("004", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-03"),
  interval("004", states[3], "2020-01-04", "2020-01-04"),
  interval("005", "0", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-10"),
  interval("005", states[1], "2020-01-01", "2020-01-10")
))
```

The two overlapping history records for `002` describe the same state.
Import combines their coverage without counting the overlapping days twice.

## Choose the weekly rules

Death takes priority over either living state. Pneumonia history takes priority
over the state without pneumonia. Both death states are absorbing, so no
further cycles are generated after a selected death cycle.

```{r configure}
studyPath <- tempfile("c2t-weekly-example-")
dir.create(studyPath)

allowed <- stats::setNames(list(
  states,
  states[c(2, 4)],
  character(0),
  character(0)
), states)

study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "WeeklyExample",
  pathToStudy = studyPath,
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = input,
  stateCohortLabels = states,
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = states[c(4, 3, 2, 1)],
  stateCohortAbsorbing = states[c(3, 4)],
  allowedStatesList = allowed,
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  lengthOfStay = 7
)
```

```{r generate, results='hide', message=FALSE}
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)
```

## Inspect the weekly histories

```{r result}
clinical <- subset(trajectories, !state_label %in% c("START", "EXIT"))
knitr::kable(clinical[c(
  "subject_id", "state_label", "state_start_date", "state_end_date"
)], row.names = FALSE)
```

For `003`, the second cycle is labelled `Death, pneumonia history`. The label
preserves the history classification even though that cycle also contained
living days before and after pneumonia. It does not retain the January 10
onset date as a separate weekly row.

For `004`, the first cycle is already a death cycle. This does not imply that
the patient died on January 1. Weekly dates describe the cycle, not the exact
onset of its selected state. Both patients' final cycles end on their death
dates here because their target intervals end on those dates. If the target
interval extended further, selecting an absorbing state would stop after its
cycle rather than shorten that cycle to the event day.

For `005`, the second cycle covers only January 8 to 10. Its `EXIT` marker is
January 11. An analysis must not interpret that marker as a death or count it
as an additional day of follow-up.

These checks run when this article is built:

```{r checks}
expected <- list(
  "001" = rep(states[1], 3),
  "002" = states[c(1, 2, 2)],
  "003" = states[c(1, 4)],
  "004" = states[3],
  "005" = rep(states[1], 2)
)
for (id in names(expected)) {
  stopifnot(identical(
    clinical$state_label[clinical$subject_id == id], expected[[id]]
  ))
}
stopifnot(
  tail(clinical$state_end_date[clinical$subject_id == "005"], 1) ==
    as.Date("2020-01-10"),
  trajectories$state_start_date[
    trajectories$subject_id == "005" & trajectories$state_label == "EXIT"
  ] == as.Date("2020-01-11")
)
```

## Rerun from the saved settings

Copy just the settings into a new location and provide fresh input. We reuse
the synthetic data to check that moving the study does not change its result.
On the server, the new input would come from that site's database.

```{r replay, results='hide', message=FALSE}
newPath <- tempfile("c2t-weekly-replay-")
newSettings <- file.path(newPath, "WeeklyExample", "Settings")
dir.create(newSettings, recursive = TRUE)
copied <- file.copy(
  file.path(studyPath, "WeeklyExample", "Settings", "analysisSettings.rds"),
  newSettings
)
stopifnot(copied)

restored <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "WeeklyExample",
  pathToStudy = newPath,
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = input,
  runSavedStudy = TRUE
)
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = restored)
replayed <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = restored)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(trajectories, replayed)))
```

No state definitions or selection rules were re-entered. Only the location
and fresh data were supplied.

## Before fitting a model

The four labels can be used as four model states. If an analysis instead treats
pneumonia onset and mortality as two steps within a week, it needs an explicit
rule for the transition from alive without pneumonia to death with pneumonia
history. A general transition estimator cannot infer that rule from the label.

Likewise, a requirement that pneumonia precede death by at least one calendar
day belongs in the analyst's cohort definitions. Do not infer that separation
from two weekly labels. Use the underlying state intervals for analyses that
need exact dates. See [Read the output](a05_output.html) for their locations.
